newsitem.title: CONGO: Fresh U.S. forces on Zaire evacuation standby.
newsitem.headline: Fresh U.S. forces on Zaire evacuation standby.

text.p: The United States rotated fresh Marines into Central Africa at the weekend and urged its nationals to leave Zaire, where rebels were marching on the capital Kinshasa.

The Marines arrived in Congo on Saturday to join French, Belgian and British troops on standby to evacuate foreign nationals from Kinshasa in the event of a battle for the teeming city or a rampage by Zaire's ragged and ill-disciplined army.

The switch -- the 22nd Marine Expeditionary Unit replaced the 26th at sea off Zaire and in Brazzaville -- coincided with failed talks off Congo between Zaire's embattled President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila.
But the spokesman for the force, Commander Robert Anderson, denied any link.
"This was planned way in advance and had nothing to do with the meeting between Kabila and Mobutu," he told Reuters.
Anderson was spokesman for U.S. forces who evacuated 2,000 foreigners from the capital of the West African nation of Liberia a year ago.

The State Department urged U.S. citizens in Zaire on Saturday to leave and warned Americans not to travel there, citing the "deteriorating security and political situation" and the "potential for unrest throughout the country."

Spokesman Nicholas Burns said the government was ordering the departure of all non-essential U.S. embassy personnel. The government earlier ordered dependents of U.S. embassy personnel to leave Zaire.
Several thousand Western nationals live in Zaire's capital of five million people -- principally citizens of France and former colonial power Belgium.
The United States has 400 nationals there, Canada 500. Anderson said the Marines would evacuate both and possibilty other nationalities.
French and U.S. military spokesmen say that their respective ambassadors in Kinshasa will give the signal for any evacuation.

The United States has the amphibious assault ship USS Kaersarge in the Atlantic off Zaire's port of Matadi in the mouth of the Zaire River. It has CH46 helicopters and larger CH53s plus Cobra attack helicopters.
"Everything we do is defensive, the Cobras are also defensive," Anderson said earlier in the week.

The Unit, based in Norfolk Virgina, has 1,400 Marines of whom 100 were in Brazzaville and the remainder on the ship together with 1,100 sailors. The Kaersarge replaced the USS Nassau off Zaire at the weekend.
Anderson said that in the event of an evacuation the ship would deploy the helicopters and bring in as many Marines as needed to secure the evacuation zone.
France has 300 troops in Brazzaville, Britain about 200 and Belgium almost 700.
The American force includes Navy special forces or SEALs, whose job is to protect the residence of the U.S. ambassador.
